articleParts.text: While a '.ship' file defines the base hull, you will often need to create specific loadouts (Variants) or modified versions of the hull (Skins) for campaigns and missions.
A Variant (.variant file) represents a specific loadout of weapons, fighter wings, hullmods, and stat distributions for a ship.
1. In the Variants instrument tab, you can create a new variant based on the active hull.
2. Equip Weapons: Select a weapon slot on the ship and choose a weapon from your game data repository to equip it.
3. Assign Weapon Groups: Group equipped weapons together and define whether they are linked (fire simultaneously) or alternating.
4. Add Hullmods and Wings: Allocate ordnance points to add passive hullmods and equip fighter wings in available launch bays.
5. Distribute remaining ordnance points into Capacitors (flux capacity) and Vents (flux dissipation).
A Skin (.skin file) represents a modified version of a base hull. For example, a Pirate or XIV Battlegroup version of a standard ship.
1. In the Skins instrument tab, you can create a new skin derived from the base hull.
2. You can specify a completely different sprite image for the skin.
3. Override base stats: Modify the ship's base ordnance points, hitpoints, armor, flux capacity, and other core statistics.
4. Manage Built-ins: Add or remove built-in weapons and built-in hullmods that differ from the base hull.
5. You can also modify weapon slot properties, such as changing a slot's type from Ballistic to Energy or resizing it.
